fields.why: The Table gives prevalences for 3+ groups of age, race/ethnicity, education, employment and income-to-poverty ratio, and the text makes t-tested claims across several of them.
Age (3 bands), race/ethnicity (6 groups) and SES (education 4, IPR 5, employment 3 compared) qualify; sex and sexual identity have only 2 groups.

Age and employment claims are t-tested against named referents (aged >=65 or 45-64; employed), and the gradient claims for education and IPR sit under a blanket 't-tests were performed' line, which the brief treats as per-group vs referent only; race/ethnicity values appear only in the Table with no claim or test, so side by side.

brief_issues: A blanket t-test line under a monotone gradient claim (education, IPR) with no stated referent could also be read as side by side; the brief's per-group vs referent rule names 'higher than most other groups' claims but not gradients.
